data.narrative:
Hybron is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Brennan Lieu and Aaron Guo that has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of nine private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

The Stage-Progression method is applicable here and forms the basis of valuation. Using total capital raised of $30M as a proxy for current value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier for progression from Seed to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $75M. The Peer-Median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables; while ten same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, clustering by stage or valuation tier did not produce the minimum three datapoints required for statistical confidence.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to the single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $64M to $86M, with a median of $75M. The low and high bounds reflect ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for this particular market and stage context, and the lack of peer-based cross-validation. Additional comparable company data at adjacent stages or tighter valuation tiers would strengthen confidence in this range.
